# Field reference

Every field of the two Airtable bases the pipeline uses, generated by `field_docs.py` on 2026-11-14 from the live schema. The text comes from the field descriptions in Airtable, which are the source: change a description there (or ask for it in a pull request) and regenerate this page.

"Who writes it": **you** = a person fills or changes it (the owner or an analyst); **robot** = a script writes it, do not edit by hand; **formula** = computed by Airtable from other fields; **Airtable AI** = an Airtable AI field that reads the cover text.

How to use the fields day to day is in [guide.md](guide.md).

## Disclosure Library (`appXS0v6SnWdzAsY3`)

### monitored_links

| Field | Kind | Who writes it | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `link_id` | text | robot | Stable id of the page (written by assign_ids.py). The join key for documents found on it. |
| `link_name` | long text | robot |  |
| `wba_id` | text | robot | The company this page belongs to. |
| `company_name` | text | robot |  |
| `url` | link | you | The page this URL is being watched at. Fix the type if it is wrong, untick monitor if it is junk, tick capture_page if the page itself is a disclosure. |
| `page_language` | pick one | robot | Values: English, Portuguese, Japanese, Bengali, Spanish, German, Italian, Dutch, Slovenian, French, Albanian, zh, Swedish, Catalan, Danish, Thai, Turkish, Korean, Indonesian, eng, fra, Kannada, in, Ukrainian, Romanian, Vietnamese, Chinese (Simplified), Hebrew, az, Croatian, ... (75 in all). |
| `type` | pick one | you | What kind of page this is. Only reports_hub, sustainability_page, sustainability_report, investor_relations and policies are harvested for documents, so a wrong type here means missed documents. Values: investor_relations, other, reports_hub, news, sustainability_page, policies, homepage, sustainability_report. |
| `frequency` | pick one | you | How often the plain monitor reads the page. Values: daily, weekly, monthly, mon_wed_fri, mon_fri. |
| `status` | pick one | robot | Last read result: ok, redirected, error or dead. Error with no HTTP code across a whole domain means the site blocks robots at connection level; escalate rather than retry. Values: ok, error, dead, redirected, blocked. |
| `http_status` | number | robot | HTTP code of the last read (200 ok, 403 refused, 404 gone). |
| `final_url` | link | robot | Where the address ended up after redirects. |
| `is_pdf` | checkbox | robot | The watched address is itself a PDF, not a page. |
| `source` | pick one | robot | How the page entered the base (company list, discovery, added by hand, approved suggestion...). Values: derived, discovered, company_list, sweep, sitemap, analyst, hub_search, added by hand, approved suggestion, research. |
| `last_checked` | date | robot | Last time a monitor read this page. The browser queue works oldest first, so an old date means the page is waiting its turn, not that it failed. |
| `content_hash` | long text | robot |  |
| `notes` | long text | you | Free notes about this page: why it was added, why monitoring was turned off, quirks of the site. |
| `seen_links` | long text | robot | Every document link ever seen on this page. This is what the harvester turns into library rows, so an empty list on a page full of documents is a collection bug worth escalating. |
| `new_links` | long text | robot | Document links that appeared on this page since the previous check, newest first with the date. This is where a fresh publication shows up first. |
| `assigned_analyst` | person | you |  |
| `report_library` | link to rows | robot | Documents harvested from this page. |
| `created_time` | created time | formula |  |
| `last_modified_time` | last modified | formula |  |
| `docs_language` | lookup | formula |  |
| `monitor` | checkbox | you | Whether the nightly monitors read this page. Untick third-party sites, job boards and other junk; the page stays on record. |
| `company summary` | Airtable AI | Airtable AI |  |
| `last_change` | date | robot |  |
| `alert_status` | pick one | robot | new = new document links since the last check. Values: new, notified. |
| `needs_browser` | checkbox | robot | The page needs a real browser to be read. Owned by the machine: do not tick or untick it by hand. |
| `certified` | checkbox | you | Tick once you have confirmed this is the right page for its type on the company's site. Your sign-off on the page layer. |
| `certified_by` | person | you |  |
| `webpage_library` | link to rows | robot |  |
| `capture_page` | checkbox | you | Tick when the page is a disclosure in itself and not just a list of files. It is then printed to PDF and archived every Sunday, with change detection. |
| `company` | text | robot |  |
| `companies` | link to rows | robot |  |
| `scan_now` | checkbox | you | Tick to scan this page now: find its documents, add them to report_library, attach the PDFs, read their covers and refresh the company's completeness. Picked up within about 10-15 minutes; unticks itself when done (see scan_status). New pages are scanned automatically, no need to tick. |
| `scan_status` | long text | robot | Result of the last on-demand scan, in plain words: when, how many documents the page shows, how many were new to the library, and anything that went wrong. Written by scan_now.py. |
| `already_listed` | long text | robot | Filled within seconds of adding a page: if the company already has this URL (ignoring http/https, www, trailing slash and tracking parameters), it says under which type and the new row is switched off so it is not scanned twice. Blank = new URL. |
| `scan_outcome` | pick one | robot | Short result of the last on-demand scan, written by scan_now.py. 'Nothing new' on a page you suspect is the signal the weekly missed-reports audit looks at first. Values: Found new documents, Nothing new, Page failed, Row needs a fix. |
| `last_manual_scan` | date | robot | Date someone ticked scan_now by hand on this page (automatic scans of new pages do not set it). A manual scan is treated as a suspicion: the weekly audit reviews these first. |
| `scan_concern` | long text | you | Optional, yours: what looks wrong with this page (e.g. 'I see the 2024 report here but it never arrives'). The weekly audit reads it, investigates this page first and answers in audit_reply. |
| `audit_reply` | long text | robot | The weekly missed-reports audit's answer about this page: what it found, why documents were missed, what it fixed or which pull request fixes it. Newest first. |
| `docs_from_page` | count | formula | Documents in report_library that were harvested from this page (discarded ones included). |
| `links_on_page` | formula | formula | How many document-looking links the monitor found on this page (lines in seen_links). |
| `possible_issue` | formula | formula | Live warning for monitored report-type pages. 'Page does not open'; 'Document links not in the library' (3+ links on the page look like documents but their documents are not held under any page of the company: see unharvested_sample); 'No document links found on the page' (possibly a JavaScript page or the wrong URL). Blank = no sign of trouble. Tick scan_now to try a fresh scan, and write in scan_concern what you see. |
| `unharvested_links` | number | robot | Written nightly by the harvester: links on this page that look like documents (PDF-shaped, confirmed PDFs, or on document-server addresses not yet checked) whose document is NOT in report_library under any page of this company. 0 = everything the page offers is held. |
| `unharvested_sample` | long text | robot | Up to 5 of those links, so you can open them and judge before scanning. |
| `delete_now` | checkbox | you | Tick to delete this page for good within minutes. It is archived first and blocked, so no robot search or suggestion ever adds it again (pasting it yourself in add_link still works). The documents already found on it stay in the library. Certified pages are never deleted. |
| `pc_checked` | date | robot | When the office-network runner (pc_fetch.py, the robot on the owner's computer) last read this page because the site refuses cloud servers. The document links it finds go to seen_links and new_links like the nightly monitor's. |
| `link_texts` | long text | robot | The text of every document link on the page, one per line: address, a tab, the link text. Written by the monitors since 4 Nov 2026; harvest copies each text to report_library.link_text. |

### report_library

| Field | Kind | Who writes it | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `library_id` | text | robot | Stable id of the document (from its normalized address). Unique. |
| `wba_id` | text | robot |  |
| `company_name` | text | robot |  |
| `document_url` | link | robot | Where the document lives on the web. Open it to check the document when the attached file is missing. |
| `doc_label` | formula | formula | The analyst-facing line: year, company and the best title we have. Built automatically. To change it, curate the title. |
| `year` | formula | formula | THE year to use. First that applies: 1) a year you typed in curated_doc_title; 2) a regulator filing's own year; 3) fiscal_year read from the full text with year_score 80+ (99% right); 4) the analyst's year for documents imported from the Source Library; 5) fiscal_year with year_score 60-79 (96% right); 6) the AI's year, only when its quote was verified in the document; 7) year_rules (title / address rules). year_source says which one was used. |
| `fiscal_year_wba` | formula | formula | WBA's reporting year of the document: a fiscal year ending 30 June Y to 29 June Y+1 is year Y (SDG2000 data collection guidance, Aug 2025). With only months known: a year end in January to May counts as the year before; June counts as its own year (changed from January to June on 4 Nov 2026, #205). |
| `year_source` | formula | formula | Which source decided year (see year's description for the order). 7 = the weakest, a guess from the title or the link. |
| `period_end` | text | robot | End of the reporting period the document covers: 2021-12, or just 2021 when the month is unknown. |
| `effective_type` | formula | formula | The type to filter on: source_type_check (AI) when set, else source_type (from the address). Same rule the coverage numbers use. Lets non-English documents, which the AI has not typed, be included. |
| `source_type_check` | pick one | you | The effective document type, decided by AI over the first pages. This is the field you correct when it is wrong. Pick UNKNOWN when the document fits none of the types. Values: Impact Report, Statutory Documents, Code of Conduct, Policy Documents, Financial Statement, CSR Report, Annual Report, Human Rights Policy, Climate Report, Environmental Reports, Company Presentations, Integrated Report, ESG Report, Registration Document, SASB Index, Engagement Report, Certifications, Interim Reports, CDP Report, GRI, Social Reports, 10K Form, Sustainability Report, UNKNOWN. |
| `source_subtypes` | pick one | you | Sub-category within the chosen type, decided by AI. Correct it only when it is clearly wrong; the type matters more. Values: 10K Form, AGM / shareholder meeting notice, AI & data ethics, Accessibility statement, Animal welfare, Annual / financial report (statutory), Annual Report, Annual return, Anti-corruption & bribery, CDP Report, CSR Report, Certifications — other, Climate & environment, Climate Report, Code of Conduct, Community & philanthropy, Community & social impact, Company Presentations — other, Corporate / about / contact, Corporate governance report, Customer, marketing & product, Diversity, equity & inclusion, ESG Report, ESG targets & data dashboard, Employees, workforce & benefits, Employment, labour & HR, Engagement Report, Environment & climate, Environmental Reports, Ethics & compliance, ... (89 in all). |
| `file` | file | robot | The PDF itself. Empty usually means the download is still pending or the site blocked it; check file_status before assuming the document is lost. |
| `file_status` | pick one | robot | Why the file could not be attached: blocked, not_pdf, too_big or gone. Filled only on failure, so blank plus an attached file is the normal state. Values: blocked, not_pdf, too_big, gone, web_document. |
| `page_count` | number | robot | Pages in the PDF (read with the cover). |
| `doc_language` | pick one | robot | Language detected from the document text. Documents outside English are collected and dated but not yet typed by AI. Values: English, Portuguese, French, Chinese (Simplified), German, Japanese, Spanish, Arabic, Russian, Thai, Korean, Vietnamese, Kannada, Tamil, Greek, Croatian, Catalan, Norwegian, Indonesian, Turkish, Hindi, Italian, Polish, Romanian, Slovak, Slovenian, Ukrainian, Czech, Dutch, Estonian, ... (55 in all). |
| `doc_scope` | pick one | you | Full document, or Section / excerpt when the file is only a chapter. UNKNOWN when deciding would cost more than it is worth. Values: Full document, Section / excerpt, UNKNOWN. |
| `sustainability_class` | pick one | robot | Where the sustainability disclosure lives (sustainability_class.py, by rules): D dedicated = a standalone sustainability/ESG/CSR/impact report; E embedded = an integrated report, or an annual report whose pages hold a substantive sustainability section; S specialized = one topic or framework (climate, CDP, GRI, policies); F financial only = no such section. Same four classes as SustainabilityReports.com. Values: D dedicated, E embedded, S specialized, F financial only. |
| `class_reason` | text | robot | Why sustainability_class was decided: the rule and the numbers (pages about sustainability, longest block, contents entry). Starts with "first pages:" when only cover_text was read; such rows are re-read once the full text exists. |
| `sustainability_share` | number | robot | Percent of the pages with text that are about sustainability (1.5 lexicon terms per 1,000 characters and 3 different terms). Full text only. |
| `frameworks` | pick several | robot | Reporting standards the document names at least twice in its full text (once on the first pages). Values: ESRS, GRI, SASB, ISSB, TCFD, TNFD, Integrated Reporting Framework, SDGs, UN Global Compact, GHG Protocol, EU Taxonomy, SBTi, CDP, BRSR, HKEX ESG Guide. |
| `discard` | checkbox | you | Removes the row from every count and queue without deleting it. Always pick a discard_reason. Untick to bring it back. |
| `discard_reason` | pick one | you | Why the row was discarded. These reasons are counted and read: they are how collection rules get fixed upstream. Add a note when you pick Other. Values: Duplicate of another document, Wrong company / misattributed, Not a disclosure, Out of language scope, Out of topic scope, File unusable, Other, Archived: before 2022, not cited. |
| `Reviewer notes` | long text | you | Free notes for anything the fields cannot express: doubts, group structures, why you chose a type. Read during pilot reviews. |
| `found_on` | link | robot | The company page this document was found on. Useful when you suspect a misattribution: open it and see whose site it is. |
| `page_type` | pick one | robot | Type of the page the document was found on. Values: investor_relations, sustainability_page, policies, reports_hub, sustainability_report. |
| `doc_year` | text | robot | Year from the rules (file name, cover, filing, address). One input to `year`; doc_year_from says where it came from. |
| `source_link_id` | text | robot |  |
| `first_seen` | date | robot | When the pipeline first saw this document. Sort by it to find what arrived this week. |
| `source_type` | pick one | robot | First-pass type guessed from the web address alone. Do not edit it: it is one of the two opinions the disagreement queue compares. Values: Statutory Documents, Code of Conduct, Policy Documents, Financial Statement, CSR Report, Annual Report, Human Rights Policy, Climate Report, Environmental Reports, Company Presentations, Integrated Report, ESG Report, Registration Document, SASB Index, Engagement Report, Certifications, Interim Reports, CDP Report, GRI, Social Reports, 10K Form, Sustainability Report, Impact Report, Other. |
| `match_confidence` | text | robot | How sure the address classifier was about source_type. |
| `source_page` | link to rows | robot |  |
| `source_title` | Airtable AI | Airtable AI | Title extracted by AI from the document cover. An "[auto]" prefix means it was constructed, not read. Blank on non-English documents, which are not classified yet. |
| `cover_text` | long text | robot | Text of the first six pages, read by build_cover_text.py. What the AI fields and most rules read. |
| `cover_status` | text | robot | Result of reading the cover: ok, or why not (no_text, parse_fail, truncated, file too big...). |
| `created_time` | created time | formula |  |
| `scope_input` | formula | formula |  |
| `verified` | checkbox | you | Tick when the row is right as it stands: right company, right type, usable title, plausible year, readable file. Verifying freezes the row against AI reprocessing. |
| `type_mismatch` | formula | formula | Flags documents where the URL guess and the AI disagree. These are the rows worth reviewing first. |
| `assigned_analyst` | person | robot |  |
| `classify_input` | formula | formula |  |
| `curated_doc_title` | text | you | Your title override. Copy the real title verbatim from the cover, without translating or shortening. It wins over everything and fixes the year too. |
| `company` | link to rows | robot |  |
| `discarded_on` | last modified | formula | When discard was last changed. The purge job deletes rows discarded more than 30 days ago, so untick discard within 30 days if a row should come back. |
| `delete_now` | checkbox | you | Tick to delete this document for good within minutes (no 30-day wait). It is archived first and blocked forever, so the robot never brings it back. You can tick many rows at once. Verified rows are never deleted. |
| `auto_title` | text | robot | Title read by the robot from the file name or the cover page, for documents the AI has not titled. Used in doc_label when there is no curated or AI title. Written automatically; to fix a title, use curated_doc_title instead. |
| `content_hash` | text | robot | SHA-256 of the PDF file's bytes (written by the robot when it reads the file). Two rows with the same value hold the exact same file. 'unavailable' = the attachment is not a PDF. |
| `file_size_mb` | number | robot | Size of the attached file in MB, written by the robot from the attachment. Very small values (under ~0.1 MB) usually mean an error page or a cut-off download. |
| `doc_year_from` | pick one | robot | Where doc_year came from (written by date_documents.py): file name = a year in the file name; cover = the reporting period printed on the first pages; address = the upload folder in the link (weakest); waiting for cover = provisional until the file's first pages are read; filing = regulator filing's own year; none = nothing found. Values: file name, cover, address, waiting for cover, filing, none, source library. |
| `fiscal_year` | number | robot | Year in which the reporting period this document covers ENDS (Source Library convention), read from the full text by fiscal_years.py. Trust it when year_score is 60 or more. |
| `year_score` | number | robot | Confidence in fiscal_year, 0-100. Checked against analysts' fiscal-year-end dates: 80+ was right 99% of the time, 60-79 about 96%, below 60 not reliable (the year formula ignores it). |
| `year_basis` | pick one | robot | What decided fiscal_year: scope = the report says what period it covers; period = 'year ended <date>' statements; title = the report title; label = FY labels / balance dates only; none = no evidence found. Values: scope, period, title, label, none. |
| `year_evidence` | long text | robot | The sentence (and page) that decided fiscal_year, so anyone can check it in the PDF. |
| `ai_year_test` | checkbox | you | Rows in the AI fiscal-year test (20 rows whose year the full-text reader could not settle). Only ticked rows feed ai_fiscal_year. |
| `ai_year_input` | formula | formula | Cover text, only for rows ticked in ai_year_test (keeps the AI test from running on the whole library). |
| `ai_fiscal_year` | Airtable AI | Airtable AI | TEST: AI reading of the fiscal year for rows ticked in ai_year_test. Format: YEAR \| PERIOD_END \| CONFIDENCE \| EVIDENCE. |
| `robot_type` | text | robot | Snapshot of the type the pipeline settled on (source_type_check when the AI had answered, else source_type), taken by qa_sync.py the first time it saw a value. Written by the robot only, never by a person. When source_type_check later differs from this, the difference is a human correction and becomes a label in Pipeline QA. |
| `robot_year` | text | robot | Snapshot of the year the pipeline settled on (the year formula at the time), taken by qa_sync.py the first time it saw a value. Robot only. A later curated_doc_title that changes the year is recorded as a correction in Pipeline QA. |
| `robot_title` | text | robot | Snapshot of the title the pipeline settled on (source_title when the AI had answered, else auto_title), taken by qa_sync.py the first time it saw a value. Robot only. A later curated_doc_title is recorded as a correction in Pipeline QA. |
| `ai_year` | formula | formula | Just the year from ai_fiscal_year (its first four characters when they are a year). Blank when the AI found none (NONE / SKIP). |
| `ai_year_verified` | checkbox | robot | Ticked by the robot when the sentence the AI quoted in ai_fiscal_year really appears in the document. Only verified AI years are used in year. |
| `year_rules` | formula | formula | Fallback year (last resort for year): the first year in the AI title, ignoring maturity dates and years after doc_year + 1, else doc_year. |
| `scope` | pick one | robot | Is this file a whole report or a piece of one? Decided by rules (doc_scope.py), no AI: page ranges or chapter numbers in the file name, section words in the title, summaries, very short files. scope_reason says which rule. Use this instead of doc_scope. Values: Full document, Part of a report, Summary or short document. |
| `scope_reason` | text | robot | The rule that decided scope, in plain words, e.g. 'page range in the file name: p108-162' or '212 pages, no sign of a piece'. |
| `assurance` | pick one | robot | External assurance of the sustainability information, as the full text states it: limited or reasonable assurance near sustainability wording (never the financial audit's "reasonable assurance"), or an assurance statement without a stated level. D, E and S documents with full text only. Values: limited, reasonable, limited and reasonable, assured, level not stated, none found. |
| `analyst_flag` | pick one | you | Set by an analyst who spotted something wrong with this document, from the Analysts interface. Nothing changes automatically: the owner reviews flagged rows and fixes them. Clear it once handled. Values: Wrong type, Wrong year, Wrong company, Only part of the report, Duplicate, File broken or missing, Not a disclosure, Other. |
| `analyst_flag_note` | long text | you | What the analyst saw, in their words: the right type or year, the page where the problem shows, the copy it duplicates. |
| `is_urd` | formula | formula | 1 when this document is a universal registration document, i.e. the annual report in France, Spain, Belgium: type Registration Document, 100+ pages, a title naming a registration document or an annual (financial) report, and no prospectus, final terms, supplement, programme or bond words. Same rule as company_coverage.py (is_urd). 0 otherwise. |
| `archive_url` | link | robot | Not used. Created for an Internet Archive retry that was measured (0 of 61 refused reports recovered from the cloud) and closed without merging (#53). Refused files are now fetched from the owner's computer (pc_fetch.py, see retry_note). |
| `retry_note` | text | robot | Written by the office-network runner (pc_fetch.py, the robot on the owner's computer) for files the site refuses to cloud servers: what happened, e.g. 'attached: downloaded from the office-network runner (browser)', 'read on the office-network runner; too big to attach (12.3 MB)' or 'still refused from the office network (status 403)'. |
| `retried_on` | date | robot | When the office-network runner (pc_fetch.py) last tried to get this refused file. Each file is tried at most once a day; recent sustainability and annual reports first, then the ones tried longest ago. |
| `ai_title` | formula | formula | source_title when it is a title, blank when the AI answered with a sentence instead ("I don't have access to the document text...", "The text provided...") or wrote more than 200 characters. doc_label uses this, so such answers never show as a title. |
| `cover_ocr` | checkbox | robot | Ticked by ocr_covers.py when cover_text was read by text recognition (OCR) from page images, because the PDF is a scan with no text. Such text can hold recognition errors. |
| `entity_check` | pick one | you | Whose report this is, read from the cover by key_reports.py (only for candidate long annual reports of the two latest publication waves): group = the cover names the company itself; subsidiary = the first legal name on the cover is a subsidiary (Finance, Funding, Capital, a country...); a subsidiary report never counts as the company's key report; unclear = no legal name found (still counts). Correct it if wrong: the robot rewrites it only when its own reading changes. Values: group, subsidiary, unclear. |
| `entity_name` | text | robot | The legal name key_reports.py found on the cover and used for entity_check, e.g. 'BMW International Investment B.V.'. |
| `key_report_latest_fin_of` | link to rows | robot | The company for which this document is the latest wave's financial key report (the other side of companies.kr_latest_fin). Written by key_reports.py; do not edit. |
| `key_report_latest_sust_of` | link to rows | robot | The company for which this document is the latest wave's sustainability key report (the other side of companies.kr_latest_sust). Written by key_reports.py; do not edit. |
| `key_report_prev_fin_of` | link to rows | robot | The company for which this document is the previous wave's financial key report (the other side of companies.kr_prev_fin). Written by key_reports.py; do not edit. |
| `key_report_prev_sust_of` | link to rows | robot | The company for which this document is the previous wave's sustainability key report (the other side of companies.kr_prev_sust). Written by key_reports.py; do not edit. |
| `pub_date` | date | robot | When the report was published, as far as the evidence shows (pub_dates.py, key report types from 2023). Precision in pub_date_precision (a month-only date is stored as the 1st), evidence in pub_date_source and pub_date_evidence. To correct it, type the right date and set pub_date_source to person: the robot then leaves the row alone. |
| `pub_date_precision` | pick one | robot | day = pub_date is the exact day; month = only the month is known (pub_date is the 1st of that month). Values: day, month. |
| `pub_date_source` | pick one | robot | What decided pub_date, strongest first: regulator filing = the SEC or ESEF filing date; publication = the document states its publication date; board approval = the date the board approved the report or authorised the accounts for issue (usually the publication day or a few weeks before); first seen = the day the robot first saw it on a page it already watched (published on or before that day); not found = full text read, no date; person = set by hand, never overwritten. Values: regulator filing, publication, board approval, first seen, not found, person, signature. |
| `pub_date_evidence` | long text | robot | The sentence (and page) that decided pub_date, e.g. 'p.142: The financial statements were authorised for issue by the Board on 27 February 2025', so anyone can check it in the PDF. 'first pages:' when it was read from cover_text, before the full text existed. |
| `evidence_profile` | long text | robot | How many passages of this report are evidence on climate, nature and social, by measurement area (planning, implementation, performance), following the grid of WBA's Integrated Transition Assessment white paper (evidence_chunks.py; reports 2024+ with full text). The passages themselves, with their page, are in the private text store (evidence-*.jsonl.gz), ready for a later extraction tool. |
| `evidence_version` | text | robot | Version of the evidence lexicon (evidence_terms.json) that produced evidence_profile. When the lexicon changes, documents are tagged again. |
| `file_created` | date | robot | Creation date written inside the PDF (document info or XMP), read by file_dates.py. Usually the day the final file was exported, days or weeks before release. A clue to the publication date, never proof: pub_dates.py uses it only when it falls after the period end and before first_seen. |
| `file_modified` | date | robot | Last modification date written inside the PDF, read by file_dates.py. Changes whenever the file is re-saved (a corrected version, a re-upload), so it can be much later than the publication. |
| `file_dates_from` | text | robot | Written by file_dates.py: where file_created and file_modified came from (pdf info, xmp), 'none' when the PDF carries no dates, or why the file could not be read. A filled value takes the row out of the queue. |
| `key_role` | formula | formula | Which key report this document is for its company, from the four key_report_* links written nightly by key_reports.py: both (it serves as the financial and the sustainability key report, for example an integrated annual report), financial, sustainability, or blank (not a key report). Used by the publication-timing charts on the Hoy interface. |
| `pub_month` | formula | formula | Month of pub_date as 01 to 12, blank when pub_date is blank. Used to chart when in the year companies publish their key reports. Dates whose pub_date_source is 'first seen' are the day the robot first found the file (it started in July 2026), not the publication day, and are left out of the charts. |
| `company_contacts` | link to rows | robot |  |
| `company_fy_end_month` | lookup | formula | The company's usual fiscal-year-end month (companies.fy_end_month), for fiscal_year_wba when period_end has no month. |
| `attribute_values` | link to rows | robot |  |
| `origin` | pick one | robot | How the document reached the library. Our discovery: the monitor, the harvest, Serper web search, the daily research, links added by hand. Source Library 2024 / 2025 / 2026: imported from the analysts' own collection (import_source_library.py), so it says the library is complete, not that our discovery found it. Blank on older rows means discovery unless the Reviewer notes say Source Library. Values: discovery, web search or research, added by hand, Source Library 2024, Source Library 2025, Source Library 2026. |
| `link_text` | text | robot | The text of the link the document was found under on the company's page ("Annual Report 2024", "Chapter 3: Environment"). Often says the type, year, scope and language better than the address. Written by harvest since 4 Nov 2026. |
| `values_also_printed_here` | link to rows | robot | The attribute_values rows whose figure this document also prints (the reverse of attribute_values.other_documents): the value was read from another document and this one prints the same company, attribute and year. Written by propose_values.py since 9 Nov 2026. Together with the `document` link's reverse, it says which values a document is evidence for. |
| `stored_file` | text | robot | Where the PDF's copy is kept in lanterN's own storage (bucket/path and size in bytes), written by archive_copy.py once the copy is uploaded and its size checked. A document is archived out of this table only when this is filled. |

### mention_searches

One row per question of the form "which companies mention X in their documents". People fill in the names to look for; the Mention search workflow (mention_search.py in wba-link-monitor) writes the result on the row and one row per matching document in mention_hits. Rules and set-up: TEXT_SEARCH.md in the repository.

| Field | Kind | Who writes it | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | text | you | Name of the search. Yours to choose; it only labels the result. |
| `result` | text | robot | Written by the run. Companies found, out of the companies that have a searchable document in scope. A company with nothing to search is left out of the share, not counted as silent. |
| `find` | long text | you | Names to look for, one per line. Any one of them counts. Whole words only. Capitals matter only for acronyms: WBA finds WBA, never wba. A star matches any ending: benchmark* finds benchmark, benchmarks and benchmarking. |
| `short_names` | long text | you | Acronyms, one per line. An acronym is ambiguous, so it counts only in a document that also contains one of the names in find, or where a confirming word stands next to it. |
| `confirming_words` | long text | you | Optional. Words that settle what an acronym means when they stand within 8 words of it, one per line (benchmark*, CHRB). |
| `near` | long text | you | Optional. Count a mention only when one of these words is within the distance below, on the same page. One per line (gender*). |
| `distance` | number | you | Most words allowed between a name and a nearby word. Blank means 25. Each hit records its actual distance, so a result can be tightened afterwards with a filter, without a new run. |
| `doc_types` | pick several | you | Only these document types. Blank means every type that has been read in full. Values: Sustainability Report, ESG Report, CSR Report, Integrated Report, Impact Report, Social Reports, Annual Report, Engagement Report, Climate Report, Environmental Reports, Policy Documents, Code of Conduct, Human Rights Policy, GRI, SASB Index, CDP Report, UNKNOWN, Interim Reports, Statutory Documents, Company Presentations, Financial Statement, 10K Form, Registration Document, Certifications. |
| `year_from` | number | you | Only documents dated this year or later. Setting a year leaves undated documents out: they cannot answer a question about a year. |
| `year_to` | number | you | Only documents dated this year or earlier. |
| `companies` | long text | you | Optional. wba_ids, one per line (PT_00123). The share is then counted inside this list. Paste the companies of a benchmark here to get the share of that benchmark's companies. |
| `look_in` | pick one | you | Full text reads every page and is the real answer. First pages reads only the first six pages of each document: quick, needs no text store, and is a lower bound. Blank means Full text. Values: Full text, First pages. |
| `active` | checkbox | you | Tick to have the search re-run every night as new documents arrive. |
| `status` | text | robot | Written by the run: ok, or what went wrong or needs attention. |
| `last_run` | date and time | robot | Written by the run. |
| `companies_found` | number | robot | Written by the run. Companies with at least one matching document, before review. |
| `companies_searched` | number | robot | Written by the run. Companies that have at least one searchable document in the scope of this search. The denominator of the share. |
| `docs_found` | number | robot | Written by the run. Documents that match. |
| `docs_searched` | number | robot | Written by the run. Documents read for this search. |
| `hits` | link to rows | robot | The documents that match this search, one row each in mention_hits. Filled by the run. |
| `companies_after_review` | rollup | formula | Companies still counted after review: distinct companies among the hit rows, leaving out rows marked Not a mention and stale rows. Updates as soon as a row is reviewed. |
| `share_after_review` | formula | formula | companies_after_review as a share of companies_searched. This is the figure to quote once the hits have been reviewed. |
| `run_now` | checkbox | you | Tick to run this search again right away (e.g. after changing its words). A new search runs by itself a couple of minutes after you stop editing it. Unticks itself; the answer arrives in result within ~10 minutes. |

### mention_hits

One row per document that matches a search in mention_searches, written by the Mention search workflow (mention_search.py in wba-link-monitor). review and notes belong to people and are never overwritten. A row that stops matching is ticked stale, never deleted.

| Field | Kind | Who writes it | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `document` | text | robot | Year, company and title of the document, as in report_library. |
| `search` | link to rows | robot | The search this row answers. |
| `company_name` | text | robot |  |
| `review` | pick one | you | Your call after reading the evidence. Not a mention takes the row out of the share. Never overwritten by a re-run. Values: Mention, Not a mention, Unsure. |
| `evidence` | rich text | robot | Up to three passages, closest first, with the matched words in bold. The page number opens the PDF on that page. |
| `pages` | text | robot | Pages of the PDF where it is mentioned. "first pages" means the row comes from a first-pages run, which has no page numbers. |
| `distance` | number | robot | Fewest words between a name and a nearby word in this document. Blank when the search has no nearby words. Filter on it to tighten a result without a new run. |
| `mentions` | number | robot | How many separate mentions the document holds. |
| `open` | link | robot | The document on the company's site, opened on the page of the closest mention. |
| `notes` | long text | you | Anything worth keeping about this hit. Never overwritten. |
| `year` | number | robot |  |
| `doc_type` | text | robot |  |
| `wba_id` | text | robot |  |
| `stale` | checkbox | robot | Ticked by the run when the document no longer matches: file replaced, document discarded, or the search tightened. Stale rows are kept and do not count. |
| `library_id` | text | robot | The document's id in report_library. |
| `hit_id` | text | robot | Search plus document. The key that lets a re-run update this row instead of adding another. Do not edit. |
| `counted_company` | formula | formula | The company id while this row still counts: not marked Not a mention and not stale. The search row counts the distinct values of this field. |
| `found_on` | created time | formula | When this document first matched the search. |

### base_health

One row per night, written by base_health.py (wba-link-monitor) at the end of the nightly run. Read-only: how full the base is, what came in and went out, which jobs failed, and how complete the company universe is.

| Field | Kind | Who writes it | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | date | robot |  |
| `status` | pick one | robot | OK, Check or Problem. Problem = a job failed or the base is over 90% full. Check = over 80% full or nothing new arrived. Values: OK, Check, Problem. |
| `attention` | long text | robot | Plain-language list of what needs you, if anything. |
| `records_total` | number | robot | All records in the base, every table. |
| `record_limit` | number | robot |  |
| `base_full` | percent | robot | records_total / record_limit. |
| `docs_live` | number | robot | report_library rows not discarded. |
| `docs_discarded` | number | robot | Discarded rows still in the table, waiting for the purge. |
| `purge_ready` | number | robot | Discarded more than 30 days ago: what the purge job would delete today. |
| `pages_monitored` | number | robot |  |
| `new_docs_24h` | number | robot | report_library rows created in the last 24 hours. |
| `discarded_24h` | number | robot |  |

Email addresses companies publish in their own key reports, one row per company and address (contacts.py, from the full text). Never deleted: an address missing from the newer reports keeps its row with an older last_seen. Personal addresses (a person's name) are marked; prefer the role mailboxes.

Values: investor relations, sustainability, media, general, ethics and compliance, privacy, people, personal, other. |

The report's own agreement with the reader: a figure printed on 2+ pages was right 76% to 88% of the time in the evaluations, a figure printed once 50% to 77%. Review the rows with 1 first. |

Empty when the two are the same. Written by propose_values.py and fix_units.py. |

## Pipeline QA (`appJQ2mRtjHjzLq9E`)

### runs

One row per script execution, written by qa.record_run() at the end of every run of wba-link-monitor (and by base_health for GitHub job status). Keyed by run_key so a re-run updates its row.

| Field | Kind | Who writes it | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run_key` | text | robot | workflow name + # + GitHub run id, e.g. 'Monitor links (daily)#39471409165'. Unique. |
| `script` | text | robot | The Python script, e.g. airtable_monitor.py |
| `workflow` | text | robot | GitHub workflow name |
| `trigger` | pick one | robot | What started the run: the cron schedule, the previous job in the chain, a manual dispatch, the scan_now watcher, or a local run Values: schedule, chain, dispatch, scan_now, manual. |
| `started` | date and time | robot |  |
| `finished` | date and time | robot |  |
| `duration_min` | number | robot |  |
| `commit_sha` | text | robot | Short commit of the code that ran. The before/after for every fix. |
| `status` | pick one | robot | ok = finished and wrote everything; partial = finished but some writes failed or the budget cut the run; failed = uncaught exception; timed_out = killed by GitHub; skipped = the workflow did not run Values: ok, partial, failed, timed_out, skipped. |
| `rows_in` | number | robot | Rows the run read or was due to process |
| `rows_out` | number | robot | Rows the run created or updated |
| `failures_recorded` | number | robot | Failure rows this run opened or touched |
| `counters` | long text | robot | JSON of the script's own counters (created, updated, blocked, unlinked, shared_dropped, promoted, slow, write_failed, ...). Free shape per script. |
| `github_url` | link | robot | Link to the GitHub Actions run |
| `notes` | long text | robot |  |
| `failures` | link to rows | robot |  |

### failures

One row per distinct failure (code + deterministic key), never per occurrence. Opened or updated by qa.record_failure() from the scripts and by qa_sync.py nightly from the Disclosure Library's status fields. A row whose key does not recur for 30 days closes as resolved_silently. OTHER is not a code: unnamed cases go to the daily review as labels with stratum unnamed.

| Field | Kind | Who writes it | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `failure_key` | text | robot | sha1 of code + the dedup key (page URL, registered domain, library_id, normalized document URL, wba_id + detail, or workflow + date, depending on the code). Unique; the upsert key. |
| `code` | pick one | robot | The failure family. Closed list: a new code is a design decision, not a data entry. Values: PAGE_UNREACHABLE, PAGE_GONE, PAGE_BLOCKED, PAGE_EMPTY, PAGE_UNHARVESTED, PAGE_WRONG_TYPE, DOC_FETCH_FAIL, DOC_UNREADABLE, DOC_DROPPED, DOC_DUPLICATE, DOC_WRONG_ROW, TYPE_DISAGREE, TYPE_MISSING, LABEL_CORRECTION, CO_GAP, CO_MISSED_KNOWN, RUN_FAILED, DOC_FLAGGED, DATA_CHECK. |
| `detail` | text | robot | The sub-cause, lower case, from the code's own list: timeout, ssl, connection, dns, nav_timeout, crash \| 401, 403, 429, challenge \| no_links, links_dropped \| blocked, gone, too_big, not_pdf, download_fail \| no_text, parse_fail, truncated \| shared, not_doc_shaped, framework_host, cross_domain \| same_hash, same_doc_key, twin_no_url, human \| misattributed, not_disclosure, out_of_scope \| high_stakes, low_stakes \| non_english, no_cover, pending, unknown \| type, subtype, year, title, language, company \| no_hub, no_sust_page, no_sust_report, no_annual_report, no_coc, no_hrp, overdue_sust, overdue_annual \| source_library, research, audit, manual_add \| job_failed, timed_out, write_failed, queue_starved |
| `severity` | pick one | robot | Computed by the writer from the severity rule: High when it hides or costs a 2023+ sustainability or annual report of the company, or blocks a whole domain; Low when it only costs money or tidiness. Values: High, Medium, Low. |
| `status` | pick one | you | open = still recurring or not yet looked at; resolved_silently = key not seen for 30 days (closed by qa_sync, with the commit range in last_commit); fixed = a named commit or PR fixed it; expected = a known limit (the site really blocks robots); wontfix = not worth it Values: open, resolved_silently, fixed, expected, wontfix. |
| `script` | text | robot | The script that recorded it, e.g. airtable_monitor.py, or qa_sync.py for failures derived from the base |
| `stage` | pick one | robot | Values: monitor, harvest, attach, cover, classify, dedupe, coverage, import, inbox, fulltext, run, analyst, reading, evidence_health. |
| `wba_id` | text | robot |  |

| `record_id` | text | robot | Airtable record id in the Disclosure Library (rec...), so a script can open the row |
| `http_status` | text | robot |  |
| `message` | long text | robot | The error text or the plain-words reason, at most 500 characters |
| `first_seen` | date | robot |  |
| `last_seen` | date | robot |  |
| `occurrences` | number | robot | How many runs recorded this key |
| `first_commit` | text | robot | Commit of the code the first time the key was seen |

| `fixed_by` | text | robot | PR number or commit that fixed it, set by the weekly review |

### labels

The golden set: one row per judged document (type, year and title on one card), or one fact about a page or company. Rows are created by qa_sample.py (the daily cards), qa_sync.py (corrections) and sl_labels.py (Source Library). On daily cards Claude (Opus) writes the answer with confidence and evidence; the owner checks about 5 a day with your_call; qa_sample.py settles every card into a label with labelled_by (Edi, Claude). Claude's labels never score the Airtable AI type. Never delete a label: an unsure one is still evidence.

| Field | Kind | Who writes it | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `target` | pick one | robot | Values: document, page, company. |

| `stratum` | pick one | robot | Why the sampler picked this case. On agreement_control rows the pipeline's type is hidden (hidden_values), from Claude and from you, to keep the measurement honest. Values: high_stakes_disagreement, non_english, agreement_control, new_arrival, unnamed, correction, source_library, audit. |
| `company_name` | text | robot |  |
| `wba_id` | text | robot |  |
| `doc_label` | text | robot | Year, company and title as the Disclosure Library shows them |
| `document_url` | link | robot | Open the document here |
| `page_url` | link | robot |  |
| `library_id` | text | robot |  |
| `record_id` | text | robot | Record id in the Disclosure Library |
| `cover_snippet` | long text | robot | First 400 characters of the cover text |

| `doc_language` | text | robot |  |
| `robot_value` | text | robot | What the URL or rule-based pass said (source_type, doc_year, auto_title, ...) |

| `suggested_value` | text | robot | Claude's answer for the type (daily labelling, Opus). Becomes true_type when you Agree, when you Disagree without correcting the type, or when the card settles with Claude's answer. |
| `verdict` | pick one | you | Optional, and you can ignore it. Which of the two opinions shown was right; it only means something when the card shows both a robot_value and an ai_value. true_type and true_year are what the evaluations count. Values: AI is right, URL is right, Both are right, Neither, Cannot tell. |
| `true_type` | pick one | you | Yours, on every card: the right type of the document, even when the robot or the AI already had it right. Same 24 options as source_type_check, plus Not a disclosure. What the type evaluations compare against. Values: Sustainability Report, ESG Report, CSR Report, Integrated Report, Impact Report, Annual Report, 10K Form, Financial Statement, Interim Reports, Registration Document, Statutory Documents, Company Presentations, Climate Report, Environmental Reports, Social Reports, CDP Report, GRI, SASB Index, Engagement Report, Certifications, Code of Conduct, Human Rights Policy, Policy Documents, UNKNOWN, Not a disclosure. |
| `true_value` | text | you | The right value for any other field (a year, a title, a language, a company, yes or no) |
| `sure` | checkbox | you | Ticked by default. Untick when you are guessing: unsure labels stay out of the evaluation set and go to the weekly review for a second opinion. |
| `reason` | text | you | Optional, one line: why. It becomes the explanation in the few-shot example. |
| `labelled_by` | pick one | robot | Values: Edi, Claude, correction, source_library, audit. |
| `labelled_on` | date | robot |  |
| `batch_date` | date | robot | The day this case was put in the review batch |
| `in_review` | checkbox | robot | On the list in Check Claude's answers. Ticked by the sampler for each new card; unticked by the daily labelling (Claude) on cards that do not need a person, and by the sampler once a card is settled. |
| `reviewed` | checkbox | robot | Ticked by the sampler when the card is settled into a label: you answered your_call (or filled true_type / true_year / title_wrong), or Claude's answer was taken because Claude left the card out or it went 3 days unanswered. labelled_by says whose label it is. |
| `split` | pick one | robot | Assigned once at creation: 70% eval, 15% fewshot, 15% regression Values: eval, fewshot, regression. |
| `failure` | link to rows | robot | The failure row this label came from, when there is one |

| `year_value` | text | robot | The year the pipeline uses for this document (the year formula), with its source, e.g. '2024 (fiscal year, score 85)' |
| `year_evidence` | long text | robot | The sentence that decided the pipeline's year (from report_library.year_evidence), so the year can be checked without opening the PDF |
| `suggested_year` | number | robot | Claude's answer for the reporting year (the year in which the period ENDS), from the daily labelling. Becomes true_year the same way suggested_value becomes true_type. Blank for documents without a period. |
| `true_year` | number | you | Yours, on every card: the right reporting year (the year in which the period the document covers ENDS), even when year_value is already right. Leave blank only for documents without a year (codes, policies). year_eval.py counts only cards where this is filled. |

| `title_wrong` | checkbox | you | Yours: tick when title_value is not the document's real title (put the real one in true_value if you want). |
| `hidden_values` | long text | robot | Robot-only: on agreement_control rows, the pipeline's type (JSON), kept out of sight so the card is blind. The evaluations read it. Do not show in the interface. |
| `your_call` | pick one | you | Yours, the one click on a card: Agree = Claude's type, year and title are right; Disagree = something is wrong, correct only that (true_type, true_year or title_wrong) and the rest is taken from Claude's answer; Can't tell = you cannot judge it (the label is kept as not sure). The sampler settles the card on its next run. Values: Agree, Disagree, Can't tell. |
| `claude_confidence` | pick one | robot | Written by the daily labelling (Opus): how sure Claude is of its answer (suggested_value, suggested_year, suggested_title). high = the cover or contents settle it; medium = one point needs judgement; low = guessing. Only low and medium cards, high-stakes ones and 2 random high ones a day stay in Check Claude's answers. Values: high, medium, low. |
| `claude_evidence` | long text | robot | Written by the daily pre-read: the decisive words quoted from the document with their page, and the type-guide rule applied (e.g. 'p.1: "Interim Report for the six months ended 30 June 2025"; rule 3: part of a year = Interim Reports; year = 2025, period ends June 2025'). |
| `check_reason` | text | robot | Written by the daily pre-read on cards it leaves for you: why this one needs a person (low confidence, medium confidence, high stakes: Claude and the pipeline disagree on a check, random audit of Claude). |

### evals

One row per scoring of one rule or prompt against the golden set. Today written by sl_labels.py (baseline scores of the address type, the AI type, the live rule and the year formula); rule changes are also measured on each pull request by year_eval.py and the coverage comparison, posted as PR comments. The ship rule: a change merges only when accuracy and high_stakes_accuracy do not fall and it fixes more cases than it breaks.

| Field | Kind | Who writes it | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eval_id` | text | robot | target @ version @ date, e.g. 'ai_type_prompt@v3@2026-11-04' |
| `run_on` | date and time | robot |  |
| `target` | pick one | robot | What was scored Values: ai_type_prompt, url_classifier, arbitration, doc_links, year_rule, dedupe, file_classifier, web search precision, cited documents held (same file), cited documents held (same company, type and year), cited documents with text in the database, elements with a quote found, narrative GMC_01930.1 Highest governance body responsible for the sustainability strategy, narrative GMC_01931.1 Highest governance body responsible for the climate strategy or transition plan, narrative GMC_01932.1 Functions, teams or committees responsible for implementing sustainability plans, page ranking ts best-of, page ranking ts single, page ranking bm25 single, page ranking bm25 best-of, page ranking learned, page ranking ts fused, page ranking bm25 fused, reader GMC_00048.1 Revenue, reader GMC_00001.1 Scope 1 emissions, reader GMC_00002.1 Scope 2 emissions, location-based, reader GMC_00003.1 Scope 2 emissions, market-based, reader GMC_00064.1 Low-carbon capital expenditure, reader GMC_02526.1 Total number of employees, narrative GMC_00685.1 Does the company have a time-bound targets on gender equality and women’s empowerment in its supply chain?, narrative GMC_00951.1 Is the statement on overtime work applicable to all company activities (own operations and supply chain or entire value , ... (125 in all). |
| `version` | text | robot | Prompt version, rule version or the name of the AI eval field used |
| `commit_sha` | text | robot |  |
| `n_cases` | number | robot | Labels used (sure, reviewed, split = eval) |
| `accuracy` | percent | robot |  |
| `high_stakes_accuracy` | percent | robot | Accuracy on the classes that move a completeness check (sustainability family, annual family, Code of Conduct, Human Rights Policy) |
| `baseline_accuracy` | percent | robot | Accuracy of the version currently live, on the same cases |
| `per_class` | long text | robot | JSON: per true class, n, correct, and the top confusion |
| `regressions` | long text | robot | Cases that were right in the live version and wrong in this one, one label_id and the two answers per line |
| `verdict` | pick one | robot | ship = passes the ship rule; hold = does not; baseline = the live version's own score Values: ship, hold, baseline, measured. |
| `notes` | long text | robot |  |
